title: Wretched Timber
text:
Wretched timber, shattered and broken,

lying chastened on the sandy beach,

abandoned by the sailor,

vile spoil of south and southwest winds.


How much better you were in the grove,

peopled with birds and branches and greenness,

before, vain and dazzled,

you went to the farthest edge of the world!


You lost the pompous freshness,

the sweet peace of the shadowed forest,

where you mocked the sounding winds.


What did your proud ambition promise itself?

To mock them also on the furious sea?

Here is the fruit of lofty thoughts.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's moral fable: a forest tree becomes shipwrecked wreckage after proud ambition.

title: A Sure Recipe
text:
Study little or nothing, and finish

the law career still a student;

go, beardless, to Madrid, and, petulant,

chatter without restraint, swindle without limit.


Write for any newspaper;

be Atlas of extreme opinions,

and rehearse your remarkable eloquence

in the cafe or in a patriotic meeting.


First try to become councilman,

and then deputy, for it can be managed

by playing a good register with skill;


Have no faith at all, and place yourself on the side

that holds the best hope of success,

and soon you will see yourself prime minister.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the satirical recipe form and the jab at opportunistic public life.

title: Divine Eyes
text:
Divine eyes, light of my soul,

for the first time I saw you angered;

and sooner would I have seen the heavens collapse,

or the cold earth open before my feet!


Have, ah, compassion on the agony

in which my senses lie buried,

when I see you sparkling and indignant

look at me, burning with impious fierceness.


Ah, forgive me if I wronged you; perhaps

I feared losing you, and with my plea and tears

instead of binding you, I only offended you more;


Have, have pity on my ruin,

for if you turn and strike me fierce again,

you will sink me into the realms of terror.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the formal appeal to the beloved's eyes and the speaker's melodramatic terror.

title: Prayer
text:
I turn the corner of prayer and burn

in a blessing of sudden sun

in the name of the condemned

I would turn back or run

to the hidden earth

but the sounding sun

purifies

the sky

Someone

finds me

Oh let him

scorch and drown me

inside his earthly wound

His lightning answers my cry

my voice burns in his hand

now I am lost in the One who blinds

and at the end of prayer the sun's clamor is heard.
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish catalog text into a compressed, prophetic English prayer.

title: Who Are You
text:
Who

are you

you who are born

in the neighboring room

so plain inside my room

that I can hear the womb

as it opens and the shadow advancing

over the ghost and the child descending

behind the wall thin as a goldfinch bone

in the bleeding room of hidden birth

for the burning and turning of time

the footprint of the human heart

does not venerate baptism

but only the shadow

when it blesses

the wild

creature
editorial_note: The translation keeps the birth-room immediacy and the narrow, breath-broken lineation of the Spanish text.
